claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Helm is open source under the Apache License 2.0 and the Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in helm/helm pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go.
Helm chart authors cannot declare dependencies between resources or subcharts, except through hook weights.

The Helm docs state that "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's hardcoded kind order begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with any kind not on the list (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-order list in reverse.
Helm sends the sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and does not wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm subchart objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so a chart cannot express installing one subchart before another.
Helm chart hooks ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations produce resources that Helm does not manage as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
In Pulumi, passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in the dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating resources that depend on it, and deploys independent resources in parallel.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.
Pulumi's dependency-ordered parallel deployment makes updates faster than a strict serial sequence.

The Pulumi Kubernetes helm.v4.Chart resource supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on resources outside it.

Helm merges objects from a chart and all its dependencies into a single set, sorts them by Kubernetes kind and applies them in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency does not make it install first.
Helm SDK is available in Go only; other languages must shell out to the helm CLI.
Pulumi Automation API is a programmatic SDK in every supported language for embedding up, preview, and destroy in a host application.

Pulumi Policies is open source with rules in Python, TypeScript, or OPA Rego; Pulumi Cloud adds centralized policy management; the Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running pulumi up.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Helm and Pulumi used together.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after the resources it depends on.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program via helm.v4.Chart or helm.v3.Release is the most common adoption pattern.
pulumi convert --from kubernetes converts rendered helm template YAML into native Pulumi code.
helm.v4.Chart renders templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object as an individual Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK, creates a real Helm release in the cluster, and preserves chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
A Pulumi program can pull charts from any Helm repository, public or private.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order with each resource ready before dependents, rather than in a fixed order by kind.
